message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively—but they share a common ancestor at the level of **class Mammalia**. In phylogenetic terms, their last shared ancestor is a member of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes many modern groups such as carnivores, ungulates, bats, and whales. The exact species of this ancestor is not known; it would have been a small placental mammal that lived sometime during the Paleogene period (roughly 66–23 million years ago).
